thread:
customer_jane: Hi team — saw a user mid-stream get cut off. They were on an iPhone tethering to an Android hotspot. Stream aborted with partial JSON and the client retried twice. Billing shows 2 partial requests charged. Anyone seen hotspot DNS flips cause this?

support_jen: Sorry about that — can you paste the raw response they got and the client logs? Also which SDK + version?

customer_jane: Here's the raw from the app console: `...{"event":"delta","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}` then socket closed with code 1006. Client log: `SSE: got EOF while parsing chunk; reconnecting (attempt 1)`. App SDK: iOS 1.4.2 + our JS layer 0.9.8.

support_jen: thanks. Do you have a repro step? Is carrier LTE->WiFi flip involved?

customer_jane: Repro is fairly consistent: iPhone connected to Android hotspot, stream starts, then toggle hotspot off/on on android -> client sees partial chunk then disconnect. Happens after ~30–45s.

oncall-bot: deploy-log @edge-proxy 2024-09-18T16:02:14Z 10.1.23.8: upstream reset (502) connection reset by peer

eng_mike: Dropping in — sounds like TCP reset triggered by NAT/DNS rebind on hotspot. When the tether changes IP or DNS, some mobile devices teardown sockets before OS hands over. Partial-chunk + 1006 fits. Can you share the full edge-proxy logs for that timeframe?

customer_jane: Sent `tcpdump -i any` from the hotspot device to our support email (pcap attached). Also uploaded mobile client debug log.

eng_mike: Got the pcap. Quick scan: we see ACKs from our server then a sudden FIN/RST from the hotspot gateway right after a DNS query for `api.redwood.example` returns new A record. Sequence:
```
SYN, ACK flow established
... tokens exchanged
DNS query -> new A (ipB)
RST from hotspot gateway -> client socket closed
server logs: 502 upstream reset (no graceful close)
```

eng_mike: Hypothesis: hotspot NAT or DNS rebind causes modem to short-circuit active TCP connection, dropping mid-chunk. Client tries SSE reconnect but stream state lost -> duplicate billing event recorded as separate request.

support_jen: Action items: 1) ask customer to enable keepalive/ping on client (short-term). 2) add server-side idempotency check for partial streams to avoid billing duplicate. 3) eng to triage proxy behavior on abrupt RST vs graceful close.

customer_jane: For client-level workaround, what keepalive interval is safe? We don't want to spam battery.

eng_mike: Try client heartbeat every 15s with small noop token: `:heartbeat:` event over SSE or a 204 fetch to /v1/ping. On iOS use NSURLSession with TCP keepalive options (SO_KEEPALIVE) + runloop to avoid background drop. Example iOS snippet: 
```
let config = URLSessionConfiguration.default
config.timeoutIntervalForRequest = 60
config.tcpKeepAlive = 15 // pseudocode; use setsockopt at socket level
```
Not ideal but reduces risk.

mobile_prod: We can also add a short server-side grace window: if a reconnect within 10s presents the same request-id, treat as resume and avoid charging twice. Will raise an Optimize ticket.

support_jen: Also confirm token TTL — if token rotated midstream, that may trigger client to reopen a new session. Can you confirm token refresh behavior at 30s?

customer_jane: Tokens are long-lived for this flow. No rotation. Confirmed.

eng_mike: Next steps for engineering: 1) collect more proxy traces around RST to verify any pattern of DNS A-record churn correlating with hotspot device NAT rebinds. 2) prototype idempotency by request-id header + short resume window. 3) doc a recommended client keepalive config for mobile-hotspot scenarios.

support_jen: I'm going to escalate to Billing to hold charge until we have resume/dedupe in place — marking this P1 for support billing review. @mobile_prod please sync.

mobile_prod: Will open ticket and tag eng on the idempotency issue. Also drafting KB article: "Handling mobile hotspot mid-stream disconnects" with repro steps and recommended client settings.

customer_jane: Thanks all — I'll try the 15s heartbeat and report back. Appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
